thread:
maria: quick q — we need a decision: what's the canonical way to start large telemetry recomputes? console button or public/internal API? thinking about routing, quotas, and clear cost UX
ben: API for automation is a must. console is fine as a surface but it should call the same API. otherwise we duplicate logic and edgecases.
dana: console needs a couple of controls though: canary %, priority lane selector, and an operator pause/abort. product wants a single-click experience but ops needs controls.
sam: routing note — replay-service should accept a priority flag (high|normal|low) and the scheduler routes high to dedicated-pool, normal to shared, low to spot fallback. preemption rules must be explicit.
maria: agree. also we need a clear upfront cost estimate in the console before you hit start. estimate tokens + $ and a confidence metric. don’t want surprise bills.
ben: API sketch (for discussion):
```
POST /v1/replays
Headers: Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
Body: {
  "selector": "org=acme,env=prod",
  "window": "2026-02-01/2026-02-28",
  "priority": "normal",
  "canary_pct": 5,
  "dry_run": false
}
Response: { "job_id": "r-12345" }
```
ben: job status endpoint: GET /v1/replays/{job_id}/status returns progress, token_estimate, shards_processed, errors.
dana: Idempotency-Key required. dry_run true should return token_estimate + sample output diffs, no quota consumption. product: dry-run is a big ask.
larry: (oops using louis) abort semantics: POST /v1/replays/{job_id}/stop should mark job aborted and leave offsets so we can resume. abort is idempotent.
louis: we should persist last_processed_offset per-shard so resume is resume-from-offset not restart. prevents double-work.
sam: console progress: exact percent is fuzzy because incoming late events change the denominator. show processed shards/expected shards + moving ETA + confidence band. e.g. "~3h (±30%)".
maria: UX note: show estimated tokens, estimated cost, and a small help link explaining assumptions (prefix caching, quantization, tokenization differences).
ben: quota rules: default concurrent replays per-org = 2. Enterprise can request higher. also a global token-per-day safeguard. the API should return 429 with explanation + retry-after if over quota.
dana: canary flow in console: start canary at 1% -> auto-validate using sample prompts -> if pass, prompt to escalate to full job with live estimated cost change. allow auto-escalate checkbox.
infra-bot: deploy notice: replay-service v2 rolling to staging now. new metrics: replay.jobs.started, replay.jobs.completed, replay.tokens. alert if job.token_estimate > 10000000 :warning:.
louis: operators need a lightweight kill-switch in console that can pause all low-priority jobs to prevent cost spikes during incidents. add to runbook.
maria: devex asks for SDK helper for backfills so customers can schedule programmatically. same API, but include helper method that does polling + exponential backoff.
ben: also need an audit log entry for any manual escalation/override (who clicked "force" on a job). GDPR + security wants that.
dana: UI mock next steps: product & design will iterate on the dialog with canary slider, cost estimate, and a small "what could go wrong" collapsible.
sam: engineering next steps: implement priority routing + idempotency, expose job status API, persist offsets, add quota checks.
louis: I'll add resume/abort endpoints and offsets. will add integration tests for idempotency semantics.
maria: OK. owners: ben (API spec + idempotency), sam (routing & quota enforcement), dana (console mock + canary UX), louis (offsets/resume/abort). checkin EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
ben: +1
dana: +1 :white_check_mark:
sam: sounds good. will prototype scheduler policy tomorrow.
infra-bot: NOTE: created ticket REPLAY-842 in backlog for quota UI and REPLAY-843 for dry-run API.
maria: thanks — leaving this thread, will sync on the EOD tracker.
